content: Dr. Philip G. Jenkins was responsible for the technical editing of the report. The Disease Reference Group (DRG) activities, including the production of this report, were funded by the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR) and financial support from the European Commission under Agreement PP-AP/2008/160-163. Taylor LH, Latham SM, and Woolhouse MEJ identified risk factors for the emergence of human diseases in their 2001 study published in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Series B. They emphasized the importance of understanding zoonotic and environmental factors contributing to disease outbreaks. The WHO/DFID-AHP Joint Meeting, with participation from FAO and OIE, highlighted the control of neglected zoonotic diseases as a critical pathway to poverty alleviation. Hotez PJ et al. (2009) discussed strategies to improve the health of the world's poorest populations by controlling neglected tropical diseases in their publication in The Lancet. Molyneux DH (2008) proposed a paradigm shift to address the other diseases of Millennium Development Goal 6, aiming for equity and poverty reduction, as detailed in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Molyneux DH (2010) questioned whether neglected tropical diseases had reached a tipping point in global health priorities in a Lancet commentary. Moran M et al. (2009) analyzed global spending on neglected disease research and development in PLoS Medicine, revealing significant funding gaps. Liese BL and Schubert L (2009) examined the allocation of official development assistance for health, focusing on neglected tropical diseases, in International Health. Molyneux D et al. explored the intersection of zoonoses and marginalized infectious diseases of poverty, emphasizing the need for integrated control strategies. Burke CM, Carabin H, and Torgerson PR contributed to the Oxford Textbook of Zoonoses (2011), detailing the health impact and burden of zoonotic diseases. Hyder AA and Morrow RH (2001) provided an overview of disease burden measurements and trends in International Public Health: Diseases, Programs, Systems, and Policies. Mathers CD et al. (2005) assessed the global status of cause-of-death data in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization, highlighting the need for improved mortality data collection. Drummond MF et al. (2005) discussed cost-utility analysis methods in health care program evaluations in their book published by Oxford University Press. Murray CJL and Lopez AD (1996) conducted a comprehensive assessment of global disease burden, mortality, and disability in their seminal work published by Harvard University Press. Budke CM, Deplazes P, and Torgerson PR (2006) analyzed the global socioeconomic impact of cystic echinococcosis in Emerging Infectious Diseases. Knobel DL et al. (2005) re-evaluated the burden of rabies in Africa and Asia in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. Harrison W (2008) quantified the burden of neglected zoonotic diseases in developing countries in Public Health in Developing Countries. Carabin H et al. (2006) estimated the cost of Taenia solium cysticercosis in South Africa in Tropical Medicine and International Health. Majorowski MM et al. (2005) conducted a cost analysis of echinococcosis in Tunisia, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. The WHO Technical Report Series No. 971 (2012) outlined research priorities for zoonoses and marginalized infections, emphasizing the economic impact of porcine cysticercosis. Zoli A et al. (2003) reviewed the epidemiology and impact of Taenia solium cysticercosis in Africa in Acta Tropica. Ito A, Nakao M, and Wandra T (2003) discussed human taeniasis and cysticercosis in Asia in The Lancet. Praet N et al. (2009) analyzed the monetary and disability burden of Taenia solium cysticercosis in Cameroon in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Rajkotia Y et al. (2007) evaluated the economic burden of neurocysticercosis in Peru in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Murthy JMK and Rajshekar G (2007) assessed the economic impact of seizures associated with solitary cysticercus granuloma in Neurology India. Croker C et al. (2010) used hospital discharge data to evaluate the economic burden of neurocysticercosis in Los Angeles County in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Torgerson PR et al. (2001) estimated the economic effects of cystic echinococcosis in Jordan, the UK, and Uruguay in the Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology. Budke CM et al. (2005) analyzed the economic effects of echinococcosis in the Tibetan Plateau in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Benner C et al. (2010) examined the economic impact of cystic echinococcosis in Spain in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. Lembo T et al. (2010) demonstrated the feasibility of canine rabies elimination in Africa using data-driven approaches in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. The WHO Expert Consultation on Rabies (2005) provided a comprehensive report on rabies prevention and control strategies. Hampson K et al. (2008) analyzed rabies exposures, post-exposure prophylaxis, and deaths in endemic regions in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Del Brutto OH et al. (2001) proposed diagnostic criteria for neurocysticercosis in Neurology. Roman G et al. (2000) advocated for declaring neurocysticercosis an internationally reportable disease in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. Sanchez A et al. (1999) conducted a clinical study on neurocysticercosis diagnosis in Honduras in Parasitology International. Ndimubanzi PC et al. (2010) systematically reviewed the frequency of neurocysticercosis in people with epilepsy in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Puri V et al. (1991) studied neurocysticercosis in children in Indian Pediatrics. Shasha W and Pammenter MD (1991) conducted sero-epidemiological studies of cysticercosis in South African schoolchildren in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology. Thomson AJG (1993) reported on neurocysticercosis cases in South Africa in the South African Medical Journal. Grill J et al. (1996) identified a high prevalence of serological markers of cysticercosis among epileptic Malagasy children in Annals of Tropical Paediatrics. Rosenfeld EA et al. (1996) studied neurocysticercosis in children in Chicago in Clinical Infectious Diseases. Talukdar B et al. (2002) examined clinical characteristics and outcomes of neurocysticercosis in children in Annals of Tropical Paediatrics. Mafojane NA et al. (2003) reviewed the status of neurocysticercosis in Eastern and Southern Africa in Acta Tropica. Gaffo AL et al. (2004) identified cysticercosis as a leading cause of partial seizures in Peruvian children in Revista de Neurologia. Carabin H et al. (2005) assessed the monetary burden of Taenia solium cysticercosis in Honduras, India, and South Africa at the American Public Health Association Annual Meeting. The International Task Force for Disease Eradication (1993) provided recommendations for disease eradication in MMWR Recommendations and Reports. The WHO (2008) developed a global plan to combat neglected tropical diseases, emphasizing integrated control strategies. The WHO (2006) outlined a strategy to estimate the global burden of foodborne diseases, emphasizing the need for improved data collection. Willingham AL and Mugarura A (2008) discussed the link between Taenia solium tapeworms and epilepsy in Uganda in International Epilepsy News. Zhou XN et al. (2008) highlighted collaborative efforts to combat neglected tropical diseases in Southeast Asia in Parasitology International. Willingham AL III et al. (2008) reported on the inaugural meeting of the Cysticercosis Working Group in Europe in Emerging Infectious Diseases. Murrell KD (2005) provided WHO/FAO/OIE guidelines for taeniosis/cysticercosis surveillance and control. Garcia HH et al. (2006) evaluated combined human and porcine mass chemotherapy for controlling Taenia solium in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. Ngowi HA et al. (2008) conducted a health-education intervention trial to reduce porcine cysticercosis in Tanzania in Preventive Veterinary Medicine. Kyvsgaard NC et al. (2007) simulated Taenia solium transmission and control using a stochastic model in the International Journal of Parasitology. Caulfield LE et al. (2004) identified undernutrition as an underlying cause of child deaths associated with diarrhea, pneumonia, malaria, and measles in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition. Brandt JR et al. (1992) developed a monoclonal antibody-based ELISA for detecting circulating antigens in Taenia saginata cysticercosis in the International Journal of Parasitology. Thomas SV et al. (2001) analyzed the economic burden of epilepsy in India in Epilepsia. Boa ME et al. (2002) studied the distribution of Taenia solium cysticerci in naturally infected pigs in Tanzania in Veterinary Parasitology. Carpio A (2002) provided an update on neurocysticercosis in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Carpio A and Hauser WA (2002) examined seizure recurrence in newly diagnosed neurocysticercosis patients in Neurology. Avode DG et al. (1996) investigated epilepsy caused by cysticercosis in Benin in the Bulletin de la Société de Pathologie Exotique. Preux PM et al. (2000) studied antiepileptic therapies in Cameroon in Epilepsia. Birbeck G et al. (2007) analyzed the social and economic impact of epilepsy in Zambia in The Lancet Neurology. Carabin H et al. (2005) assessed the infection burden of cysticercosis and echinococcosis in Trends in Parasitology. Praet N et al. (2009) evaluated the disease burden of Taenia solium cysticercosis in Cameroon in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Jenkins DJ et al. (2005) provided a global update on the emergence and re-emergence of Echinococcus spp. in the International Journal of Parasitology. Brunetti E et al. (2010) developed expert consensus guidelines for diagnosing and treating cystic and alveolar echinococcosis in humans in Acta Tropica. Torgerson PR et al. (2010) assessed the global burden of alveolar echinococcosis in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. Craig PS and Larrieu E (2006) reviewed the history of cystic echinococcosis control from 1863 to 2002 in Advances in Parasitology. Chen MG (1993) discussed the epidemiology and clinical aspects of Schistosoma japonicum infections in Human Schistosomiasis. Carabin H et al. (2005) estimated the sensitivity and specificity of diagnostic methods for Schistosoma japonicum in the Philippines in the International Journal of Parasitology. Wang TP et al. (2005) studied the transmission of Schistosoma japonicum by humans and animals in China in Acta Tropica. McManus DP et al. (2010) reviewed schistosomiasis in China during the era of the Three Gorges Dam in Clinical Microbiology Reviews. Finkelstein JL et al. (2008) estimated age-specific disability weights for Schistosoma japonicum in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. McGarvey ST et al. (2006) examined associations between animal and human Schistosoma japonicum infections in the Philippines in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization.
